design.quote: In this retrospective file audit, the clinical records of all patients admitted to our referral poisoning hospital with the diagnosis of methadone intoxication between May 2016 and March 2018 were reviewed.
design.text: retrospective case series of methadone‑intoxicated patients

findings.quote: Methadone intoxication was defined based on history, clinical presentations of respiratory depression (opioid toxidrome) or loss of consciousness (LOC) responsive to administration of naloxone, as well as detection of methadone in urine analysis.
findings.text: Methadone can be detected in urine analysis of intoxicated patients.

ref.title: Characterizing post-mortem blood concentrations in methadone-related deaths

sources.title: Characterizing post-mortem blood concentrations in methadone-related deaths
money: Open access funding provided by Alma Mater Studiorum - Università di Bologna within the CRUI-CARE Agreement. Not applicable.

design.quote: A systematic literature review was conducted to retrieve and analyze publications on methadone-related deaths that included post-mortem toxicological analyses.
design.text: Systematic literature review and forensic case series of methadone‑related deaths

findings.quote: We observed that the average blood concentration of methadone found in adult cases is 503 ng/mL, higher than observed in children, and overlapping with the range of concentration normally reported in living patients undergoing MMT (400–1000 ng/ml).
findings.text: Methadone can be detected in blood at concentrations that overlap with therapeutic levels in living patients.

findings.quote: Post-mortem methadone concentrations detected in cases of fatal methadone intoxication can overlap with those found in living intoxicated individuals or in patients undergoing maintenance therapy.
findings.text: Post‑mortem blood tests can detect methadone at levels similar to those in living patients.

limits.quote: great heterogeneity in the reports of methadone-related deaths and deaths involving methadone, making it difficult to identify demographic susceptibilities or a concentration cut‑off beyond which death from methadone is considered likely.
limits.text: The heterogeneity makes it difficult to define a concentration cut‑off for lethal methadone levels.
